label: copy-phase z input, later in recall, when the next output is z or e
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input is z (99.9% of activation mass). This is a z that was just copied back, so in_first=0. Only about 5% of copy-phase z inputs fire. Two things gate it: (1) position, since it is silent at recall_idx <= 2 and its rate rises with recall_idx/t, with most mass at recall_idx 3-7; (2) the token being output, since it is strongest when out_tok is z (44% of mass) or e (33%), and much weaker for t/o/j/f. The top activations are z followed by z or e in the original (e.g. ...q z z e...). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on non-z inputs (except a few weak hits on e). Missed activations are mostly weak ones: z inputs where the output is some other token. The false positives are mostly z->z/e steps at recall_idx 3-4 in shorter sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+7.76), in_tok=z (+4.58), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+3.74), out_tok=z (+3.56), phase=2 & out_tok=e (+3.29), out_tok=e (+3.15). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.22), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.15), recall_idx=1 (-3.15), next_out=i (-2.30).
